key_insight: DSGNAR is a scalable second-order training framework that tackles the core PINN bottleneck—severe optimization ill-conditioning—by combining doubly-sketched Gauss-Newton updates with adaptive control of regularization and step size.
engineering_relevance: It enables PINNs to reach near round-off accuracy much faster and more reliably, making them more practical for high-accuracy PDE solving in scientific and engineering workflows.
method: Doubly-sketched Gauss-Newton model for scalable second-order optimization
Adaptive ratio strategy to control regularization and step length
Designed to improve conditioning across nonlinear, chaotic, multi-scale, and high-dimensional PDE problems
evidence_signal: Across a benchmark suite including Burgers', Poisson, and Navier-Stokes problems, the method achieved relative L2 errors as low as 3×10^-16 in double precision and strong speedups, including sub-10-second single-precision Burgers' training to 4.75×10^-7.
watch_item: As a second-order, sketching-based optimizer, performance may depend on implementation details, precision choice, and problem structure, so reproducibility and memory/compute overhead should be validated for new PDE settings.
paper_title: An Optimisation Framework for the Well-Conditioned Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks
